title: Compound Risk: Homogeneity + Supply Chain Concentration = Single-Vendor Systemic Exposure

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: correlating supply chain concentration with output homogeneity quantifies a real systemic risk. Directly useful for deployers and regulators.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Intermediate: mapping supply chains from public documentation is research-accessible. Correlating with output similarity requires the Artificial Hivemind data but is analytically straightforward.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Sustained effort: mapping the full AI supply chain (compute, annotation, inference) is a broad data collection task, though it could be narrowed to one supply chain dimension.

novelty.reasoning: The conceptual link between AI supply chain concentration and systemic risk is well-documented in governance and risk management literature. However, no existing work empirically correlates supply chain concentration metrics with measured output homogeneity (e.g., from the Artificial Hivemind dataset). The compound risk framing combining both dimensions is partially but not fully addressed.

evidence.finding: IAPP documents the hidden fragility of AI supply chains and how traditional risk management fails to capture concentration risk when multiple vendors share the same foundation model.
Risk Ledger describes how two vendors may pass individual assessments yet both rely on the same sub-supplier, creating hidden single points of failure.

evidence.source: Swept AI - AI Vendor Risk in Financial Services
evidence.finding: Documents fourth-party concentration risk: five different AI vendors built on the same foundation model provide less diversification than they appear to.
